Order 
The first and the ninth accused in S.T. No. 80 of 1991 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Neyyattinkara, have filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 16 (1) (a) (i)
r/w Section 2 (ia)
(a) (m), 7 (i) and 17(1) (a) (ii) (b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
2.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Neyyattinkara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard.

3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
The first accused was the Secretary of Dhavala Viplava Charitable Society, Karode.
The first accused was also the salesman and the board member of the ninth accused Society.
Accused Nos.2 to 8 were also the board members of the society.
On 28.5.1991 at about 3 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, Neyyattinkara purchased 900 ml. of cow milk from the first accused.
After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.
After analysis, the report was received from the Public Analyst stating that the sample analysed did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow milk and hence the same was adulterated.
On the request of the accused, the second sample was sent for analysis to the Central Food Laboratory.

Ext.C1 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the Central Food Laboratory also found that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow milk under the PFA Rules and hence the same was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts.P1 to P24 series were marked for the prosecution.
Ext. C1
was also marked.
DW1 was examined and Ext.D1 series were marked for the revision petitioners.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.C1 certificate cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.

The learned counsel for Dharmamony vs The Food Inspector on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26504022/
2

the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v.
Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text:
Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v.
Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee)
and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext.C1 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra)
that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this revision petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 16 (1) (a) (i) r/w Section 2 (ia) (a) (m), 7 (i) and 17(1) (a) (ii) (b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bonds of the revision petitioners stand cancelled and they are set at liberty.

Sd/-
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl/08.01.2016
